name: Botulax / Hutox / Meditoxin

lead: Botulax, Hutox and Meditoxin are botulinum toxin type A brands from South Korean makers. People use them abroad to smooth wrinkles and to slim the jaw by reducing masseter bulk, giving a narrower, smoother lower face.

Type A toxins block acetylcholine release at the neuromuscular junction, relaxing the injected muscle so lines soften and masseter bulk gradually shrinks. Botulax contains letibotulinumtoxinA and Meditoxin (also Neuronox) was developed by Medy-Tox. Trials mostly compare them with Botox for wrinkles, and the masseter use has been studied in smaller datasets. No studies of Hutox are in the literature reviewed.

paras: Clinicians inject the wrinkle areas or the masseters in a short visit, and people repeat sessions as the effect fades over months. Jaw slimming shows gradually over weeks as the muscle reduces in size.

They are prescription injectables with temporary effect. A 2020 review states that clinical evidence on the purity and immunogenicity of Nabota, Meditoxin/Neuronox and Botulax is limited, and any foreign protein can provoke immune reactions.

angle.text: These Korean toxin brands smooth wrinkles and slim the jaw by reducing masseter bulk, the draw for people wanting a narrower lower face. The toxin relaxes muscles so lines soften and the masseter gradually shrinks. Trials mostly compare them with Botox for wrinkles, with masseter use studied in smaller datasets.

lead: Botulax, Hutox and Meditoxin are botulinum toxin type A products from South Korean makers. Botulax contains letibotulinumtoxinA, and Meditoxin (also marketed as Neuronox) was developed by Medy-Tox.[1][2][3] They are used for wrinkles and, in studies, for masseter hypertrophy, spasticity and blepharospasm.[3][4][5]
A 2020 review states that clinical evidence on the purity and immunogenicity of Nabota, Meditoxin/Neuronox and Botulax is limited.[1] Hutox is named in this entry but no studies of it were reviewed.

paras: A double-blind randomized trial of 60 intention-to-treat patients compared Meditoxin with Botox in essential blepharospasm.[3] A randomized phase III trial tested letibotulinumtoxinA (Botulax) in post-stroke upper limb spasticity,[5] and another in children with cerebral palsy.[6] A pilot study examined Botulax in chronic occipital neuralgia.[7]
Registered trials include Botulax versus Botox in glabellar lines (n=262), crow's feet lines (n=240) and benign masseteric hypertrophy (n=80).[8][9][10]
Reviewers note that all protein therapeutics are potentially immunogenic, that protein quantity matters, and that formulation data are not always public.[1][2]
Comparative randomized trials exist for Meditoxin and Botulax in medical conditions,[3][5][6] and registered trials cover cosmetic indications.[8][9][10] No studies of Hutox were reviewed.
